messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated 5xx rate detected in eu-west1 gateway cluster starting 2026-03-15T09:12:08Z. Metric: gateway.5xx_rate > 6% over 5m (baseline 0.3%). Affected routes: /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings. Auto-escalation: paging oncall.
oncall-alex: oncall here, I'm seeing the same. Routing spike toward eu-west1, 95th latency climbing, and a subset of requests returning 504 gateway timeout. Paging SRE and runtime.
sre-jordan: looking. Querying edge logs and gateway pool status now. Any deploys in last 30m? I see a canary rollout for dedicated pool id dp-euw-3 at 09:02.
eng-runtime-leah: yes, we rolled a quantized runtime patch to dp-euw-3 at 09:05 for kernel pinning. It was a staggered canary (5% traffic). No immediate errors reported in CI. Could the new runtime cause slow cold starts for certain model sizes?
oncall-alex: note: customer-impact alert triggered for high-error-rate customers: several enterprise tenants in EU reporting degraded responses. product-ops-maya, can we surface status page note? Keep it minimal until we confirm.
product-ops-maya: ack, I'll prepare interim status: "We are investigating increased error rates in EU; some requests may fail or time out. No data loss expected." Posting in 2m.
sre-jordan: pulling proxy logs. Pattern: 502/504 responses correlate with backend worker OOM/restarts and repeated 429->retry loops in front. Also seeing a spike in KV-cache misses from prefix cache eviction events around 09:04.
infra-ryan: KV-store (redis-shared-eu1) reported an eviction storm due to memory pressure starting ~09:03. We've got eviction logs consistent with a TTL misalignment from earlier housekeeping job.
eng-runtime-leah: that matches — the new runtime increases KV usage for model kvcache prefetch under certain sequence-length heuristics. If redis evicted keys, workers repeatedly reconstruct large KV contexts and spike CPU/memory.
sre-jordan: immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop canary rollout (block further merges to dp-euw-3); 2) shift traffic for non-EU SLA tiers from eu-west1 to fallback us-east1 pool for ~10-15m to reduce pressure; 3) scale up redis-slave nodes and adjust maxmemory-policy to volatile-lru temporarily.
oncall-alex: executing step 1 now: rollback canary via deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated for dp-euw-3 canary (deployment id canary-2026-03-15-0905). Rolling back 5% -> 0% traffic. Status: completed.
oncall-alex: step 1 done. Applying routing rule to steer non-SLA traffic. eng-runtime-leah, can you prepare the routing policy patch? Use route tag "fallback-us-east-temp" and exclude enterprise tenants.
eng-runtime-leah: patch ready. Applying to gateway router set R1. Command:
```
rtctl apply --router euw-gw --policy fallback-us-east-temp --match "tier!=enterprise" --action route:us-east1
```
eng-runtime-leah: applied. Verifying..
sre-jordan: observing traffic shift now. Non-enterprise 95th latency dropping in eu-west1; overall 5xx rate starting to fall from 6% -> 1.8% over 2m.
cust-success-tom: I've messaged the affected enterprise customers that we're investigating and that enterprise traffic is on dedicated pools not impacted by the routing change. Some customers still reporting intermittent timeouts.
oncall-alex: next: scale redis and change eviction policy. infra-ryan, can you run the quick scale? We need +2 nodes and set maxmemory-policy to allkeys-lru temporarily.
infra-ryan: scaling redis-shared-eu1: adding nodes redis-eu1-03 and redis-eu1-04. Applying maxmemory-policy=allkeys-lru.
infra-ryan: scale started. ETA ~3m.
sre-jordan: also throttling prefetch on runtime: lowering kv-prefetch window env var PREFETCH_WINDOW from 8->3 for dp-euw-3 workers via config flag. eng-runtime-leah, can you push config override to active nodes?
eng-runtime-leah: pushed override to dp-euw-3 active nodes and canary rolled back so it only applies to existing worker processes. Confirmed env now PREFETCH_WINDOW=3.
infra-ryan: redis nodes up and policy changed. Observing cache hit rate recovering. OOMs/restarts on workers dropping.
sre-jordan: 5xx rate now 0.9% and trending down. Latency tail also improving. Recommend holding routing rule for 10m then gradually shift back.
oncall-alex: agreed. Keeping policy in place for 12m. Product, support — prepare comms: timeline, impacted endpoints, mitigation steps, and ask customers to retry.
product-ops-maya: compiling. Also recommend adding note that a runtime KV prefetch/config change contributed and that a postmortem will follow.
cust-success-tom: logged all customer reports and attached hit URLs & timestamps to the incident doc.
eng-runtime-leah: follow-up actions before close: 1) revert PREFETCH heuristics change as a code change with more validation; 2) add a circuit breaker fallback in worker that serves empty KV when redis miss rate > X for Y seconds to avoid rebuild storms; 3) add canary guard that monitors redis eviction metrics before applying rollout.
sre-jordan: creating an incident ticket and tagging runbook. Escalation: if 5xx > 2% after 20m, open P1 and notify execs.
oncall-alex: marking incident as mitigated but not resolved. Will monitor for next 60m. Thanks everyone, great coordination. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident update: mitigation actions applied: rollback canary, temporary routing policy, redis scale & policy change, runtime PREFETCH_WINDOW override. Current 5xx rate 0.7% (2026-03-15T09:42:08Z). Incident state: monitoring.
eng-runtime-leah: adding logs snippet for the problematic worker stack trace:
```
[09:03:57Z] worker-87 pid=4212 OOMKilled while allocating 120M for kv_rebuild
[09:04:01Z] restart policy triggered, restart_count=1
[09:04:12Z] prefetch triggered for prefix user-12345 seq_len=2048 keys=120
```
product-ops-maya: initial status page posted. Will update when incident is resolved or if customer-impact changes.
sre-jordan: creating post-incident checklist + timeline and will invite eng-runtime & infra to the postmortem. Closing the paging loop with oncall after 1h if stable.
oncall-alex: closing paging for now. If you see any regressions ping me. Good job team.
